methods.name: hello
methods.description: The handshake; must come first on every connection. Another product, or a protocol range that does not overlap the server's, is refused with `SHED_VERSION`.

methods.name: run
methods.description: Start a terminal. `name` defaults to the first free `tN`; `keep` brings it back as a shell in its cwd after a server restart; `rows` and `cols` default to `$SHED_SIZE` (`RxC`) of the server, else 50x200. ACP: `mcp_servers` (stdio, `http`, `sse`, in ACP's shapes) go to the agent; their env and header values are never saved or shown. `meta` (an object) goes unchanged as the session's `_meta`. `no_hibernate` keeps the agent running when idle. `mem_max_mb` (default the server's `$SHED_MEM_MAX`, e.g. `4G`) limits the process tree's memory, and a `mem-limit` event (with `notify`, a `[shed] <name> mem-limit …` line to the parent) says what was ended: on Linux with a user systemd that has the memory controller the program runs in its own scope with `MemoryMax` and the kernel ends a process (the agent's children are ranked first); elsewhere, once the tree is over for two samples in a row, the sampler ends the largest process the agent started (SIGTERM, SIGKILL 2 s later), and an agent over it by itself is only reported. The sampler is a guard against sustained use, not a hard limit: a fast allocation can pass it between samples. `warm` takes the ready spare session of the same recipe (agent, command, cwd, policy, MCP servers, meta, size), renamed to `name` with these labels, and starts the next spare; spares are listed as `.warm-N`, at most `$SHED_WARM_MAX` (default 2) of them, each killed after `$SHED_WARM_IDLE` seconds (default 600) unused. `parent` links it to the terminal that started it: when the parent's program ends the child is killed too, unless `outlive`; with `notify` a `[shed] <name> blocked|error|exited …` line is typed into the parent (a prompt for an ACP parent) when the child blocks, errors or ends, once per piece of news, held while the parent reports `working`.

schema.description: The terminal's name, unique per server; `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
Labels, `k=v`.
The working directory (absolute).
Come back as a shell after a server restart.
Report `idle` after this many seconds without output, until the program reports a state.

The program and its arguments; with `acp`, the agent's ACP adapter (empty: the installed
agent's), which the server wraps in its own bridge.
ACP: the model, in the words of the agent's record for the driver the server picks.
ACP: the effort, one of the record's `efforts`.
Variables for the program, over the server's own. Kept in memory only; never saved or shown.
The ACP agent the program bridges (`shed run --acp`): `read` renders its transcript.
ACP: how the bridge answers permission requests (default `ask`).

ACP: continue this session (`$SHED_ACP_RESUME` to the bridge): shed's transcript of it is replayed, then
the agent loads it (`session/load`).

ACP: MCP servers for the agent, in ACP's shapes: stdio `{name, command, args, env}`, or
`{type: "http" | "sse", name, url, headers}`. Kept in memory only; send them again to resume.

ACP: the session's options, sent unchanged as `_meta` on `session/new` and `session/load`;
which keys exist is the agent's business. Callers: drover (herdsman#923) and cooee.
ACP: never hibernate the agent when idle.
ACP: take this recipe's ready spare session if there is one, and keep a spare ready for the next run.
The most memory the terminal's process tree may hold, in MB; default the server's `$SHED_MEM_MAX`, else none.
Start it on this machine, over its held link (`machine.links`).
The terminal that started it (`shed run` sends `$SHED`).
Rows; default the server's `$SHED_SIZE`, else 50.
Columns; default the server's `$SHED_SIZE`, else 200.

methods.name: send
methods.description: Paste text into the terminal, then press enter: bracketed when the program has turned bracketed paste on, unless `no_paste`; no enter with `no_enter`. Sends go in one at a time, each whole. ACP: the text goes to the bridge as it is.

methods.name: attach
methods.description: Take over the terminal. After the response the server writes a redraw (clear, then the screen text) and the program's raw output, and closes the connection when the program's PTY closes. The client sends only notifications from then on (`terminal.input`, `keys`, `resize`); detaching is closing the connection.

schema.description: The terminal's name.

methods.name: state
methods.description: Report the terminal's state (`working`, `blocked`, `done` or `error`) with an optional note; a program can also print `ESC ] 7501 ; state=<s>[;note=<n>] BEL`, which never reaches the screen. The terminal also speaks the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501, revision 0.4): `state=<s>[:<key>=<value>]…` with `idle` and `clear`, `id`, `kind`, `progress`, `app` and base64 `title` and `msg`, and answers the probe `ESC ] 7501 ; ?`. A report with an `id` is a record of its own (`records`); on exit `working` and `blocked` ones are dropped.

schema.description: The terminal's name.
`working`, `blocked`, `done` or `error`; `idle` from OSC 7501 or the `idle_after` fallback.

The other agent's escape the state came from, e.g. `jan-osc9999`; absent for shed's own.

OSC 7501's record path, e.g. `build/tests`; absent for the terminal's own.
Why it is blocked: `permission`, `question` or `auth`.
Percent done, 0–100, while working or blocked.
The program's stable name, e.g. `make`.
A short label (OSC 7501's `title`, decoded).
A one-line description (OSC 7501's `msg`, decoded).

methods.name: wait
methods.description: Answer once the reported state is one of `until` (`idle` too, from the `idle_after` fallback; `blocked` only of `kind`, if given) or a visible screen line matches the pattern `output` (`matched`), the program exits (`exited`) or `timeout` seconds pass (`timeout`). The server blocks; nothing polls. With `children`, `name` is a parent: `all` matches once no child is working (`terminal` is the parent), `any` on the next child that reports `done`, `blocked` or `error`, or exits (`terminal` is that child; `exited` when no child runs).

schema.description: The terminal's name; with `children`, the parent's.
Wait on the terminal's children instead of the terminal.
Reported states that end the wait.
With `blocked` in `until`: only a block of this kind (`permission`, `question` or `auth`) ends the wait.
A pattern (`.`, `[…]`, `\d \w \s`, `( | )`, `* + ? {n,m}`, `\b`, `^ $`) that ends the wait when a screen line matches.
Give up after this many seconds; none waits for ever.

methods.name: events
methods.description: Stream events. After the response the server writes one event per line (see Events) for the terminals carrying every one of `labels`, first those after `since` still kept (the last 4,096 events other than `text`, and each terminal's last 256 `text` chunks), and never closes the connection; closing it unsubscribes. When events after `since` are gone it first writes `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"reset","params":{"seq":N}}`: those up to `N` are lost. A client more than 4,096 events behind gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"lagged","params":{"seq":N}}` and the connection is closed; it resumes with `since`. A connection that sent `heartbeat` gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"heartbeat"}` lines when idle.

schema.description: Only events of terminals carrying every one of these labels.
Replay the kept events whose `seq` is above this one first.

methods.name: heartbeat
methods.description: Keep the connection alive. Once a connection sends one, the server closes it when nothing comes from it for 30 s (two missed beats of 15 s), and writes a `heartbeat` line every 15 s into its idle `events` stream. A write the client does not take within 30 s also closes any connection.

slash `commands`, `[name, description, hint]`; its last `usage`: `used` and `size` of the context window in
tokens, and the `cost` when sent); `parent` names the terminal that started it (absent without one), with
`outlive` and `notify` as `run` set them.

oneOf.description: The tree's memory or CPU moved by more than 10 % since the last such event.

process.description: The process over it: the largest the agent started, or the agent's own when it started none.

ended_by.description: `kernel` (the terminal's scope) or `shed` (the sampler) ended it; `none`: the agent's own, only reported.

oneOf.description: The process tree passed its memory limit.

agent.description: The bridge's to the server: the agent's own pids as the turn began; never in the event stream.

oneOf.description: ACP: a prompt started a turn.
ACP: a chunk of the agent's reply.

title.description: What the tool does, in the agent's words.

kind.description: ACP's tool kind (`read`, `edit`, `execute`, …), when the agent sends one.

locations.description: The paths ACP's `locations` name in this update.

raw_input.description: ACP's `rawInput` in this update, left out over 4 KiB.

oneOf.description: ACP: a tool call started or changed.
ACP: the agent's plan, as it sent it.

id.description: The request's id, which `shed approve --request` names.

call.description: ACP's `toolCall` as the agent sent it, without `content`.

oneOf.description: ACP: the agent asks to run a tool; `shed approve` answers with one option.
ACP: a permission request was answered (by `shed approve` or the `--policy`).
ACP: the session is ready, or its model or slash commands changed.
ACP: the agent's context window use and cost changed (`usage_update`).

Event.description:
An event names its terminal, carries its labels and its `parent` (absent without one) and counts up in
`seq`; `event` is `started`, `state` (the reported state changed), `exited` (by itself, with its `code`),
`killed` (by `kill`), `resources` (memory or CPU moved by more than 10 % since the last one) or `mem-limit`
(the tree passed `mem_max_mb`; `ended_by` is `kernel`, `shed` or `none`).

An ACP terminal (`shed run --acp`) adds its agent's events, emitted by its bridge: `turn` (a prompt), `text`
(a reply chunk), `tool_call` (started or changed), `plan`, `mode`, `approval_request` (answer with
`shed approve`), `approved`, `reply` (the turn's whole reply and its `stop_reason`), `session` (the session
is ready, or its model or slash commands changed) and `usage` (the agent's `usage_update`: tokens `used` of
the context window's `size`, and its `cost`). A resumed session's history (`run` with `resume`) comes first, from
shed's own transcript, its events marked `"replay": true` so a client does not count them as new; what the
agent replays is dropped. An idle agent hibernates (state `hibernated`, its processes stopped); the next
send wakes it on the same session.

seq.description: The screen's change count it shows; pass it as `since` when watching again.

full.description: Every row is in `lines` (the first update, and after a resize).

cursor.description: The cursor's row and column, from 0.

ScreenUpdate.description:
`screen.watch` writes one update per line. `seq` is the screen's change count; `rows`, `cols`, `cursor`
(`[row, col]`, from 0) and `scrollback` (lines) are always there; `lines` holds the rows that changed, each
as runs of cells with one pen: `fg` and `bg` (a palette index 0–255, or `[r, g, b]`; `null` is the default),
`bold`, `italic`, `underline` and `inverse`. Trailing blank default cells are dropped, so a blank row has no
runs. `full` marks an update that carries every row: the first, and the one after a resize.

runs.description: Its cells, in runs of the same pen; trailing blank default cells dropped.

Run.description: Consecutive cells with the same pen; `null` colours are the terminal's defaults.

Color.description: A colour: a palette index (0–15 the named colours, up to 255 the xterm palette) or `[r, g, b]`.

at.description: When it was taken, unix seconds.

disk_free_mb.description: Free space on the volume of the state file, MiB.

terminals.description: Terminals by state: the reported state while running, else `running`; `exited`.

history.description: The kept samples (one a minute, 24 h) after `since`, oldest first.

MachineStats.description: `machine.stats` result: a sample taken now, and the kept ones after `since`.

at.description: When it was taken, unix seconds.

disk_free_mb.description: Free space on the volume of the state file, MiB.

terminals.description: Terminals by state: the reported state while running, else `running`; `exited`.

Sample.description: One sample of a machine's health.

error.description: Why it is down: the last connect's error.

Link.description: One machine's held link, as `machine.links` reports it.

oneOf.description: Never connected, or refused (another version); retried with backoff.

code.description: The exit code, or 128 + the signal that ended it.

Span.description: A span of lines, 1-based and inclusive.

Lang.description: A file's language, by its extension.

name.description: Its name: an identifier, an impl's `Trait for Type`, a heading's or table's text.

Symbol.description: One symbol of an outline: lines are 1-based and inclusive, `start` the first comment or attribute above it.

oneOf.description: A Markdown heading or a TOML table.
A line at column 0 with deeper lines under it, in a language shed has no rules for.

files.description: The files with a match, in name order, paths relative to `root` with `/`.

groups.description: The lines by the symbol that holds them; empty with `count`.

scope.description: The symbols around the lines, outermost first; empty at top level.

text.description: The line as it is in the file, without its line end.

clipped.description: `text` is only the line's first 4,096 bytes.

length.description: With `clipped`, the line's full length in bytes.

source.description: Where the record came from: `built-in` or the user file's path.

medians.description: The medians of its last sessions' timings, when any session got a first token.

AgentInfo.description: One `agents` entry: an agent shed has a provider record for, installed, or both.

id.description: The ACP agent id (`shed agents add <id>`).

agent.description: The PTY agent's name, as `shed setup` takes it.

auth_failures.description: Text in a line that says the login expired.

limit.description: Text in a line that says a usage limit was hit.

resets.description: Markers in a limit line that the reset time follows.

status.description: The command that shows whether it is logged in.

config_dir_var.description: The variable that moves its config folder.

settings_var.description: The variable that names its settings.

install.description: The command that installs the program.

token_var.description: The variable that carries a login token.

models.description: The models a start may name: id and name.

model_args.description: The adapter's arguments that set the model, `{model}` standing for the pick.

model_env.description: The variable that sets the model, where the adapter takes one.

effort_args.description: The adapter's arguments that set the effort, `{effort}` standing for one of `efforts`.

rules.description: The screens that set its state, for a terminal labelled `agent=<agent>`.

quota.description: Where its prompt responses' `_meta` carries the turn's tokens.

cache.description: How long its prompt cache lives on each login.

stream.description: The stream driver's data: the agent's own JSON-lines mode.

Provider.description:
What shed knows about one agent, as data: a built-in file, overridden key by key, or added, by a file of
the same name in `<config>/providers/` (`docs/acp.md`).

file.description: Its config file, under the home folder.

events.description: Each hook event and the state it reports.

id.description: Its name; `get` shows `rule:<id>` as the state's `from`.

priority.description: The highest matching rule wins; the agent's own report has priority 0.

region.description: How many of the screen's last non-blank lines it looks at.

any.description: The texts it matches, any one of them.

version.description: The agent version its golden screen was captured from.

Rule.description:
A screen rule: while one of `any` shows in the last `region` non-blank lines of the screen, the state is
`state`. Above priority 0 it outranks the agent's own report; at or below, it applies only without one.

path.description: The keys from `_meta` down to the object of counters.

Quota.description: The keys of a turn's tokens in a prompt response's `_meta`.

plan.description: Seconds on a subscription plan, the login without an API variable.

api_vars.description: Variables that, set and not empty in the agent's environment, mean an API key.

Cache.description: The prompt cache's lifetime on a plan and on an API key, and the variables that mean an API key.

oneOf.description: Its own JSON-lines mode, by the record's `stream` table, when a lane can be served whole.

DriverKind.description: The driver a provider's lanes run on.

command.description: The agent's command line, before the arguments of one start.

adapter.description: Text that names the ACP adapter when it is the last argument of a caller's own command.

launchers.description: The words an adapter is started with; `command` replaces them and the adapter.

new.description: The arguments that start a session under the id shed made (`{session}`).

resume.description: The arguments that start the agent on a session it has (`{session}`).

model.description: The arguments that set the model (`{model}`).

effort.description: The arguments that set the effort (`{effort}`).

mcp.description: The arguments that pass the MCP servers (`{file}`: a private file with the wire's text).

policy.description: Each policy's arguments; a policy without an entry stays on ACP.

meta.description: Each `--meta` option's flag, by its dotted path; an option without an entry stays on ACP.

tools.description: Each tool's ACP kind and the input key that is its title.

plan.description: The tool, and its input key, whose list is the plan.

Stream.description: How the stream driver starts an agent in its own JSON-lines mode.

distribution.description: The distribution it came from: `binary`, `npx` (installed once with npm, run by `node`) or `uvx`.

cmd.description: The ACP adapter's command line (`env K=V …` first when the registry sets variables).

sessions.description: How many sessions they are over.

Medians.description: An agent's medians over its last `$SHED_MEDIAN_OF` (default 20) ACP sessions that got a first token.

limit.description: The first line that says a usage limit was hit (the state `rate-limited`).

resets.description: The reset time that line gives.

auth.description: The first line that says the login expired.

Matched.description: `agents.match` result: the lines the agent's rules find.

title.description: The first prompt's first line, at most 80 characters.

updated.description: When its last turn ended, else when it started, unix seconds.

turns.description: How many turns it has had.

transcript.description: The transcript's path; filled in by `agents sessions`, not stored.

SessionRecord.description:
A session shed ran, `sessions/<id>.json` beside the state file: `agents sessions` lists these, `run
--resume <id>` continues one. Its transcript is `sessions/<id>.jsonl`; in a file name each byte of `id`
outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` is `%XX`. Kept `$SHED_SESSIONS_KEEP` days (default 30) after its last turn; `rm`
of its terminal deletes both at once.
